# Best Dentists in Paraguay for Expats

Paraguay has emerged as a dental tourism destination offering world-class care at 60-70% less than US prices. The best clinics in Asunción feature English-speaking staff, Swiss titanium implants, German ceramics, and specialists trained in Brazil, the US, and Europe. For expats, this means access to premium dental care without the premium prices.

## How We Selected

- English-speaking dentist or staff
- Modern technology (CAD/CAM, 3D imaging)
- Location in safe, expat-friendly areas
- Transparent pricing (no "gringo tax")
- Verified patient reviews
- Specialist qualifications

## Pro Tips

- 1Book via WhatsApp - it's the standard communication method
- 2Implant total cost includes surgery ($585) + crown ($550)
- 3Ask for itemized pricing upfront to avoid surprises
- 4Bring previous X-rays if you have them
- 5Premium clinics accept USD cash and credit cards
- 6For complex work, get a second opinion - specialists are affordable

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much do dental implants cost in Paraguay?

A complete dental implant (surgery + crown) costs approximately $1,100-1,500 in Asunción, compared to $3,000-5,000 in the US. This includes Swiss titanium fixtures and quality crowns.

### Are there English-speaking dentists in Asunción?

Yes, several clinics cater specifically to expats. Risus Dental, MediDent (Dr. Claudia), and Clínica Codas all have fluent English speakers. Always confirm when booking.

### Is dental care in Paraguay safe and quality?

Top clinics use the same materials (Swiss implants, German ceramics) and sterilization protocols as US/European clinics. Many dentists trained abroad. Stick to recommended clinics in expat areas.

### What if I have a dental emergency in Paraguay?

Odontología 3 operates 24/7/365 with locations across Asunción. Emergency consultations cost $25-40. Keep their number saved: 021 200 175.

### Should I get dental insurance in Paraguay?

Optional but affordable. Odontología 3 offers "Vanguard" prepaid plans for ~$15/month covering most procedures. Given low cash prices, many expats pay out-of-pocket.

### How do I pay for dental work?

Most clinics accept cash (USD or Guaranies) and credit cards. Some offer payment plans for major work. Always get an itemized invoice for insurance claims.
